title: Eight-unit-cell electronic modulations in cuprates originating from local molecular orbitals
authors: Zhiheng Yao, Sixuan Chen, Jianfa Zhao, Shusen Ye, Weixiang Qu, Ning Xia, Yuling Dai, Luchuan Shi, Hongrui Zhang, Zhenqi Hao, Changqing Jin, Shuo Yang, Yayu Wang
abstract: The pair density wave (PDW) state with eight-unit-cell (8a0) periodicity has been widely regarded as the primary order in cuprates, yet its existence and origin remain subjects of intense debate. Using spectroscopic imaging scanning tunneling microscopy, we observe spatial modulations of the electronic states with approximately 8a0 periodicity in both the superconducting and insulating regimes of hole-doped Ca2CuO2Cl2 cuprate. We find that the 8a0 spatial patterns are generated by the formation of molecular orbitals by doped holes, which organize into 4a0*4a0 plaquettes as the basic unit. Our results identify the 4a0 molecular orbital as the fundamental electronic building block in cuprates, while the 8a0 PDW represents a spatial subharmonic that emerges at sufficiently high doping.
summary: This research uses STM experiments and MCMC simulations to investigate the origin of the 8a0 electronic modulation in cuprates. The authors argue that this modulation arises fundamentally from the self-assembly of molecular orbitals structured around a 4a0 plaquette unit. This provides a strong real-space picture for the charge order, distinguishing it from conventional pairing theories.
main_problem: The paper investigates the origin and nature of the eight-unit-cell (8a0) electronic modulation observed in cuprate superconductors, aiming to determine if it is the primary order or a secondary feature.
main_result: The 8a0 modulation is proposed to be a spatial subharmonic arising from the self-organization of molecular orbitals built upon a fundamental 4a0 x 4a0 plaquette unit, rather than solely from finite momentum pairing.
method: The study combines experimental spectroscopic imaging scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) measurements with theoretical modeling using Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) simulations.
model_or_system: The physical system is hole-doped cuprates, studied across the insulator-superconductor phase boundary. The theoretical model treats the plaquette as the elementary degree of freedom, governed by an energy functional incorporating impurity and nearest-neighbor interaction terms.
key_observables: 8a0 spatial modulations observed in dI/dV maps, Fourier transform peaks at q ~ 1/8, and the correlation between 8a0 and 1.3a0 modulations.
important_parameters: Hole doping levels (p=0.03, p=0.05, p=0.10), and simulation parameters like g_beta and W.
main_assumptions: The 8a0 modulation is not tightly bound to well-defined d-wave pairing, and the $4a_0 	imes 4a_0$ plaquette is identified as the fundamental building block.
figures_summary: Figures show dI/dV maps revealing stripe- and ladder-shaped molecular orbital patterns, and FT analyses confirming both 4a0 and 8a0 periodicities, with simulations mapping the phase diagram dependence on interaction parameters.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first presenting STM evidence of 8a0 modulations in both superconducting and insulating regimes. It then develops a theoretical framework using plaquette models and MCMC simulations to explain the 8a0 periodicity as a subharmonic of the 4a0 molecular orbital structure, confirming this mechanism through parameter sweeps.
why_interesting: The work provides a detailed real-space mechanism for charge ordering in high-Tc superconductors, linking it to local orbital physics rather than purely momentum-space pairing theories, which is relevant for understanding emergent collective electronic states.

FIG. 4. Monte Carlo simulation illustrating the emergence of 8a0 modulations from the self- organization of 4a0 molecular orbitals. (a) Impurity potential generated by randomly distributed dopants for p = 0.05. (b) Representative low-temperature configurations of 4a0 plaquettes, showing the formation of plaquette chains. (c) The line profiles along the corresponding FT (inset), revealing the dominant 4a0 periodicity and the accompanying 8a0 modulation. (d) to (f) The same set of results as in (a)-(c) for p = 0.10. The plaquette chains become longer because of the increased coverage of molecular orbitals. Both the 4a0 and 8a0 periodicities are clearly observed.
